title: A random Lipschitz function detecting jumps
summary: Recently, A. Tyulenev and the author studied the class of metric spaces $\mathcal{X}$ such that for every mapping $γ\colon [0,1]\to\mathcal{X}$, there exists a $1$-Lipschitz function $F\colon \mathcal{X}\to \mathbb{R}$ that catches the total variation of $γ$, i.e. such that $\operatorname{V}_{F\circγ} \gtrsim \operatorname{V}_γ$. In this short note, we show that a metric space $\mathcal{X}$ enjoys this property if and only if there exists a random $1$-Lipschitz function $f$ on $\mathcal{X}$ such that $\mathbb{E} |f(x) - f(y)| \gtrsim ρ(x,y)$ for every $x$ and $y$ in $\mathcal{X}$.
